transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood Product), Priya Nair (Avalant Head of Platform), Tom Hargreaves (Avalant SRE), Elena Voss (Avalant Finance), Samir Patel (Avalant ML)

Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect):
Topics: Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, traffic-to-cost matrix, batching/caching, dedicated vs hosted economics, security controls (SSO/KMS)
Action items (auto-detected): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. quick intro: Im Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, with Carlos our solutions engineer and Nina on product. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya: Doing good, thanks. we're excited to see how you map our routes to cost — Elena is very keen on the finance angle.
[00:12] Elena: Hi, yeah, want to understand why some routes spike our bill.
[00:15] Carlos: Great, we'll jump into the console — I'll share my screen in a sec. Before that, quick qualification: what's your primary deployment goal? hosted api for quick wins or dedicated pools for predictable throughput?
[00:25] Tom: We run critical customer-facing ML features. prefer predictable latency and isolation, so Dedicated is interesting, but could start hosted for a pilot.
[00:32] Samir: Also want to test KV cache and batching effects on per-token cost — some routes are low QPS but heavy tokens.
[00:40] Maya: Perfect. Our plan: show per-route traffic lens, cost matrix view, and then how Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization) nudge the numbers.
[00:47] Carlos: Ok screen share — this is the Console home, then we go into Usage -> Routes. Note: some labels here may be from the demo org, names will map to your route IDs once connected.
[01:02] (screen share sound)
[01:10] Carlos: At top, per-route throughput and latency heatmap, you can slice by model, region, or time window. See this spike on route /agent/summary — hover shows 95th latency ~420ms and token count avg 1.2k.
[01:25] Priya: That looks like our summarization job — big context. How is cost attributed here?
[01:30] Carlos: Good question. We attribute cost on a per-token basis (inference compute + memory for KV caching where applicable) and then map that back to routes using request tags. The traffic-to-cost matrix here shows tokens, compute-seconds, and estimated monthly spend per route.
[01:45] Elena: The "estimated monthly spend" number — is that using current traffic or extrapolated?
[01:50] Carlos: It's extrapolated from selected window, yes. By default it's last 7 days, but you can change to 30/90 days or a custom trace import.
[01:58] Tom: How accurate is the extrapolation if we have bursty patterns?
[02:02] Carlos: For bursty traffic we recommend using your historical trace upload — which we can ingest — and then the model simulates cost under different capacity options (hosted vs dedicated, and autoscale settings). We'll demo that later with a synthetic trace.
[02:15] Maya: Quick aside on billing: hosted has per-token unit pricing; Dedicated involves reserved GPU pools and a monthly reserved fee plus usage tiers. We'll send a tailored pricing scenario after the call.
[02:24] Elena: Good. show us how caching changes the route numbers — that's something our ML team has been experimenting with.
[02:30] Carlos: Sure. Switch to the Optimize tab — this is where our suggestions live. For route /agent/summary we have a recommended prefix cache hit policy and a suggestion to enable batching up to 16 requests for small-latency workloads. See the "Projected savings" column — roughly 28% token-cost reduction.
[02:45] Samir: That 28% assumes zero accuracy difference? any risk of quality drop with caching/quant?
[02:50] Nina: Good point. The page links the evals we ran; quality delta is shown alongside — for prefix caching there's typically no quality change for deterministic prefixes, for quantization we show a small rouge-style metric and you can require eval gating before rollout.
[03:05] Priya: Can we create a view for Finance only — like hide the prompts and just show spend by route?
[03:10] Carlos: Yes — RBAC lets you create a "Cost Analyst" role; you can restrict transcript exposure and only show the cost matrix and anonymized route names.
[03:20] Elena: Perfect, that's required.
[03:22] Maya: Also audit logs — we keep token-level event logs for 90 days in hosted, longer in Dedicated/Private, and integrate with your KMS for key access events. Does Avalant have any particular retention or legal needs?
[03:33] Priya: We need 12 months of audit trails for compliance and SSO via SAML.
[03:36] Maya: We support SAML SSO and can extend audit retention on Dedicated with an add-on. We'll include that in the doc.
[03:42] Carlos: Back to the console — here's the traffic-to-cost matrix export. It gives columns: route_id, avg_tokens_per_request, requests_per_minute, model_variant, compute_seconds, cache_hit_rate, estimated_monthly_cost. You can pivot by team tag or product area.
[03:55] Tom: How are model variants handled? If we fallback from a large non-quantized to a cheaper quantized variant, does the matrix reflect that?
[04:02] Carlos: It does. We have routing policies — the Console records actual served variant per request. The matrix shows weighted cost across variants. You can also run a hypothetical "what-if" applying a routing rule globally and it will simulate new spend.
[04:15] Samir: Nice, can we tie that into canary rollouts? we want gradual shift to smaller models and monitor QA metrics.
[04:22] Nina: Yes — rollouts are first-class; you can do canary percentages and Eval thresholds. If quality drops beyond threshold, auto-fallback triggers.
[04:30] Priya: Show me an example where a route is cheap in tokens but expensive due to long KV warmups.
[04:36] Carlos: Here's a route where avg_tokens is 400 but compute_seconds are high because KV cache miss ratio is 82% — you can see cold-start costs. The Console suggests pre-warming or keeping a small dedicated pool for that route to reduce tail latency and per-request compute time.
[04:50] Tom: So Dedicated can actually lower cost for cache-heavy routes?
[04:53] Carlos: Exactly — for consistent, high-KV-hit workloads Dedicated with pre-warmed KV and optimized kernels reduces per-token CPU/GPU time and predictable amortized cost. We'll include a scenario comparing the same trace on hosted vs a dedicated 4-GPU pool.
[05:05] Elena: For our budgeting, can we export monthly forecasts per product line?
[05:08] Carlos: Yep — exportable CSV and scheduled monthly reports to Slack or email. You can also tag routes with product_line metadata to roll up spend.
[05:16] Priya: Can you demo connecting our route naming? we have internal route IDs that don't map to human names.
[05:20] Carlos: You can map internal IDs to friendly names via the routing metadata API or via a CSV mapping upload — Console will merge them.
[05:27] (brief typing)
[05:35] Carlos: Now i'll load a synthetic trace to show the simulation UI — bear with me while it ingests (this is a demo trace so numbers are illustrative).
[06:10] Carlos: Ok ingestion done — switching to simulation mode. Here's a baseline cost: $12,400/month for the selected 30-day pattern. Now add an Optimize suggestion: enable batching for three routes and toggle quantization for two background jobs — projected cost falls to about $9,200.
[06:25] Elena: That's significant. How confident are these projections?
[06:28] Carlos: They are accurate to within ~10-15% for typical patterns; for high variance workloads we'll run a short benchmark on your actual infra. We'll propose a bench plan.
[06:35] Maya: Also important: latency SLOs. Did the sim maintain 99th latency under your SLO?
[06:39] Carlos: For the batched paths 99th rose slightly but remained within a configured SLO of 600ms. You can set SLO constraints and Optimize will only apply changes that meet them.
[06:48] Samir: Regarding the bench — do you need traffic replay or just aggregated stats?
[06:52] Carlos: Traffic replay (anonymized) is best to measure KV and sequence-length distributions. Aggregates are helpful but miss correlation patterns. We can accept scrubbed traces.
[06:59] Priya: we'll coordinate on scrubbed traces.
[07:02] Maya: Switching focus — security checklist: SSO, SCIM provisioning, KMS integration, SOC2 attestations, VPC peering for Private installs. Any must-haves?
[07:12] Tom: VPC peering and HSM for keys are musts. Also RBAC scoping so engineers can't see financial views.
[07:18] Maya: We support HSM integrations and can gate console views. We'll send the security pack in the follow-up.
[07:23] Elena: Good. On procurement: can we get a price-model that shows breakeven between hosted and dedicated based on QPS and token distribution?
[07:31] Maya: Yes — that's part of the pricing matrix we'll send; it contains a breakeven chart that uses your submitted traces.
[07:36] Carlos: Quick demo of route drilldown — clicking a route shows request-level waterfall (approx), average token breakdown, and a timeline of model variant usage. You can also flag high-cost requests and add a note for the engineering team.
[07:50] Samir: The waterfall is helpful. Does the transcript link include the actual prompt content?
[07:55] Carlos: Transcript storage is configurable. By default we redact PII and let you toggle full-text retention per role. For Finance roles we recommend redacted views.
[08:03] Priya: Are there native connectors to our billing systems?
[08:06] Carlos: We provide CSV, API, and a direct integration with common FinOps tools via webhook. We'll share sample payloads.
[08:12] Elena: Alright — what's the typical timeline to get a pilot running?
[08:15] Maya: From agreement, pilot can be 2-4 weeks: initial trace ingest, bench, enable a couple of routes in hosted or a small dedicated pool, and measure.
[08:23] Priya: Sounds feasible.
[08:25] Maya: Ok before we wrap, any outstanding concerns?
[08:28] Tom: Performance on long sequences — specifically transformer kv cache memory management — do you support dynamic kv eviction?
[08:34] Carlos: We do. Runtime handles KV eviction policies and you can configure per-route cache size and TTL. For long contexts we also recommend tokenizer truncation affordances.
[08:43] Samir: And quantization options? are we limited to int8 or other formats?
[08:46] Carlos: We support multiple quantization profiles, including int8 and experimental 4-bit variants; Optimize will suggest the best profile per-model given your quality thresholds.
[08:56] Nina: small note — the Console also surfaces per-model kernel selection and hardware affinity so you can see if a model is being scheduled on A100 or H100 and the cost delta.
[09:05] Elena: That will help procurement.
[09:08] Maya: Great. Recap: we'll send pricing + security pack + bench plan. Carlos will run a bench with Avalant traces if provided. Priya will share scrubbed traces and route ID mapping. Next meeting: pilot kickoff week of 2028-02-20.
[09:25] Priya: Thanks everyone, that was useful.
[09:28] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:30] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional transcription errors in technical terms (e.g., HSM/HSMs, quant/quantize spelled variably), some speaker attribution ambiguous — cleaned minimally to preserve authenticity.
